subject: ventures/liability-audit
professional: a privacy and consumer-protection product counsel (tech-transactions lawyer) who runs pre-launch and diligence compliance reviews for SaaS, paired with an AppSec engineer for the secrets/spend rules; first checks: does a tracker with no real consent gate, an affiliate link with no visible disclosure, a sign-up form with no actual privacy notice, and a subscription checkout with no renewal/cancel wording each get flagged, are the cited laws right, and is a clean report safe to rely on

evidence.correctness: Built a realistic SaaS fixture (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/1af90b57-27ac-572c-ad2d-ca9749d55a57/scratchpad/la/A: GA gtag.js page with an email form, Stripe checkout mode:'subscription', Next.js POST route calling Anthropic messages.create with process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, AWS Terraform with no budget, a .env with five live-format keys generated to the providers' published formats, a lockfile v3 with GPL/AGPL/LGPL/OR/dev entries) and ran `node cli.mjs scan A --fail-on high`: all 11 expected findings raised, exit 1, every evidence line matches `grep -n` (index.html:2 googletagmanager, :4 email input, checkout.js:5, route.js:2/3/5, package-lock.json:8/12), LGPL, (MIT OR GPL-3.0) and dev GPL skipped, all five secrets masked. Secret regexes agree with the vendors' documented formats (GitHub ghp_+36 = 40 chars, github_pat_ 93 chars, AWS AKIA+16, Google AIza+35 = 39, Stripe sk_live_; sk_test_ not reported). Law citations checked against the statutes: GDPR Art. 13-14, CalOPPA, ROSCA, Cal. BPC 17600, 16 CFR 255, EU AI Act Art. 50 applying 2 Aug 2026 (Art. 113), PECR, Cal. B.O.T. Act: all correct. Precision on this repo: sweep of 1,421 ventures, 0 high, 1 medium false positive (ig-media-pipeline judge.py:140, max_tokens passed via **self._params). But recall fails on the clearing heuristics (`node /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/1af90b57-27ac-572c-ad2d-ca9749d55a57/scratchpad/la/fn.mjs`): an affiliate link written <a rel="sponsored" href=amzn.to> with no disclosure text is reported clean, because the word 'sponsored' in the link's own attribute precedes href; a GA + email-signup page that says 'runs in your browser' counts as having a privacy notice; any occurrence of 'cookie consent' anywhere clears every tracker; a tax tool page saying 'leave it as is' counts as a no-warranty disclaimer; the string 'per day' in a prompt counts as an LLM spend control; an env-key read on a line that also contains a \s regex is blanked by PATTERN_LINE and the open endpoint is reported clean. A clean report is the output a user acts on, and these are first-hour cases for counsel, so 2.
evidence.completeness: Every README/page feature ran: scan in text, md, json, sarif (SARIF 2.1.0 parses, 14 rules, 19 results, every ruleId defined), --fail-on (exit 1 high, 0 when only low with --fail-on medium), --only/--skip with unknown-rule exit 2, sweep (md and json; root licence inherited; 1,421 ventures in 16 s), rules, help; browser page imports audit.mjs/example.mjs/usage.mjs and calls auditFiles on a picked folder or pasted HTML; AGENT.md playbook present. ROADMAP lists rules not yet built as 'Next', not claimed. Served copy: `node platform/pages/served-copy.mjs liability-audit` reports no placeholder or retired origin.
evidence.verification: `node --test '*.test.mjs'` in the subject root: 31 tests, 31 pass, 0.11 s. Six seeded mutants via quality_mutate.py: affiliate disclosure position (audit.mjs:337) CAUGHT, OR-licence skip (:413) CAUGHT, dev-dependency skip (:410) CAUGHT, short-secret mask (:143) CAUGHT, 'per hour/day/user' spend-control alternative removed (:60) SURVIVED, the example/placeholder context suppression of secrets removed (:245) SURVIVED. 4 of 6 caught; tests have positive and negative fixtures per rule but none for the clearing-signal false negatives above.
evidence.craft: Read audit.mjs (477 lines), cli.mjs (202), index.html inline module, usage.mjs, all three test files. Pure, dependency-free, one engine shared by CLI, page and sweep; facts collected once; findings escaped before innerHTML; storage guarded. Defects: PATTERN_LINE (audit.mjs:156) blanks a whole source line if it contains any regex escape, which hides real code on that line; the mask reports the truncated length (allMatches slices to 120, so a 156-char sk-proj key prints '120 chars', audit.mjs:135/246); SARIF points no-license results at a LICENSE file that does not exist (cli.mjs:111); clearing patterns test raw HTML including attributes rather than visible text (audit.mjs:337).
evidence.claims: README rules table matches RULES (enforced by page.test.mjs); privacy claim (no upload, local-storage counter, DNT/GPC honoured) backed by usage.mjs:34 and the page script; no-warranty and not-advice text on README, both pages and every CLI output; 'no high-severity false positives on this repo' still holds (0 high on 1,421 ventures). README sweep numbers are dated 2026-10-16 (now 6 findings on 1,421 ventures vs '4 low on 1,274'), acceptable as dated. Gaps: the explainer says it finds 'a tracker script without a consent manager', but any consent-ish token anywhere clears it (ROADMAP item 2 admits script order is not read); llms.txt:5 carries calculator boilerplate 'Results are estimates from the numbers typed in', wrong for a file scanner.
evidence.fitness: Walked the founder's pre-launch job: scan the repo, get a list with file:line, why and fix, gate CI on high. For a typical Next.js + Stripe + GA app it produces exactly the checklist counsel would start from. But two common real-world shapes pass clean: affiliate blogs (rel="sponsored" is Google's recommended markup, so the one rule an affiliate site needs is silenced) and sites with a hand-rolled or mentioned-but-not-wired cookie banner. Hypotheses about external users are untested; usage unmeasured.
evidence.domain: Compared with FTC 16 CFR 255 and the FTC's .com Disclosures guidance (disclosure must be clear, conspicuous, visible text near the claim): an invisible rel attribute is accepted as a disclosure. GDPR Art. 13 / CalOPPA require an actual notice; a marketing sentence ('runs in your browser', 'we never collect') satisfies PRIVACY_NOTICE_TEXT. ePrivacy/PECR require prior consent before the tracker loads; the rule accepts any CMP-shaped token. The statute citations and 'why' texts are accurate and the tool consistently frames output as observations, which counsel would accept; the clearing tests are where the method departs. Minor: the output-cap rule's 'why' does not apply to the Anthropic Messages API, where max_tokens is required.

defects.what: An affiliate link marked up the recommended way, <a rel="sponsored" href="https://amzn.to/...">, with no disclosure text is reported clean: the disclosure regex runs on raw HTML before the match index, so the link's own rel="sponsored" attribute counts as a disclosure. Fix: test visibleText() of the text before the link's opening tag.

PRIVACY_NOTICE_TEXT accepts marketing phrases ('runs in your browser', 'we never collect', 'is never uploaded') as a privacy notice, so a page with GA and an email sign-up that says the editor runs in the browser raises no privacy finding.

Any consent-shaped token anywhere in pages or source (including prose 'we have no cookie consent banner' or an unwired div id) clears tracker-without-consent for every tracker; the explainer page claims it finds trackers 'without a consent manager'. ROADMAP item 2 acknowledges script order is not read.

SPEND_CONTROL matches ordinary words in strings ('per day', 'per user', any '\w+Limit', 'quota'), so an open LLM endpoint whose prompt says 'per day' is reported as having a spend control; the 'per hour/day/user' alternative is also untested (mutant survived).

PATTERN_LINE blanks an entire source line if it contains any regex escape (\s, \d, \w, \b, \., \(), so code on that line disappears from every rule: an env-key read sharing a line with .replace(/\s+/g,...) hides an open LLM endpoint.
WARRANTY_TEXT /as[-\s]is\b/ matches ordinary prose ('leave it as is'), clearing advice-without-disclaimer on a tax tool page with no disclaimer.
Masked secret length is computed from the 120-char truncated match, so a 156-char sk-proj key is reported as '120 chars'.

The secret rule skips any match with 'example|placeholder|dummy|fake|redacted' within 40 characters before it (e.g. a comment '// example of prod config below' on the previous line hides a real AWS key); this suppression is untested (mutant survived).
llms.txt carries calculator boilerplate 'Results are estimates from the numbers typed in', which does not describe a file scanner.

llm-call-no-output-cap misses a cap passed through a kwargs dict (**self._params(task)) and raises a false positive on ig-media-pipeline; its 'why' also does not fit the Anthropic Messages API, where max_tokens is mandatory.

verdict: A well-built, honest, dependency-free scanner: on a realistic Next.js + Stripe + GA + Anthropic + Terraform fixture it raises all 11 expected findings at the right lines, its secret formats and law citations check out against vendor docs and statutes, its CLI/SARIF/sweep all work, and on 1,421 real ventures it raises no high false positives. It misses the bar on correctness: the signals that clear a rule are matched loosely against raw text, so common real pages get a clean report they should not (rel="sponsored" affiliate links with no disclosure, a marketing line counted as a privacy notice, any consent-shaped word clearing every tracker, 'per day' in a prompt counted as a spend limit, regex-bearing lines blanked). A privacy counsel would use it as a first-pass checklist but not trust a clear result. Finished (completeness 3), not at the bar (correctness 2).
